objective: Replace the current opaque, end-of-recording cleanup path with a measurable and fidelity-safe S1-mini pipeline that removes deterministic grammar and punctuation rewriting, prevents common English words from being canonicalized as code, incrementally cleans committed streaming transcript chunks on Apple Metal, and keeps final stop-to-paste latency bounded for long dictations.
end_state: English streaming dictation is cleaned by S1-mini using its exact trained prompt with Styling formal, Structure lists, Context general, temperature-zero greedy decoding, and forced Metal offload. Ordinary prose never acquires catalog-driven ALL-CAPS tokens. Cleanup begins from stable ASR commits while recording, results are assembled in source order, only the unresolved tail remains at stop, every model rejection or fallback is explicit and observable, and measured quality, latency, memory, and ASR coexistence gates pass on the target M1 8 GB machine.
non_goals: Do not claim or build rich Markdown headings, bold text, links, summaries, or arbitrary instruction following; S1-mini only supports prose and conservative lists.
Do not send the 5,000-line normalization, styling, or programming JSON catalogs inside the model prompt.
Do not add an unbounded worker pool, duplicate model weights per worker, or promise a token-per-second number without measuring it on the target machine.
Do not redesign the Journal or settings UI; only expose truthful cleanup lifecycle and degraded-state information using the existing surfaces.
Do not change non-English behavior beyond preserving its current safe fallback path because S1-mini is English-only.
Do not modify the optional explicit cloud AI cleanup feature or turn S1-mini into a general prompt-rewriting model.
Do not commit or redistribute the GGUF weight file; it remains an installed runtime asset covered by the existing downloader and license obligations.

environment.language: Rust 2021 backend with strict TypeScript/React frontend
environment.runtime: Tauri 2.11.5, transcribe-cpp 0.2.0 streaming ASR, llama-cpp-2 0.1.154 with Metal
environment.package_manager: Bun for frontend commands and Cargo for Rust commands
environment.os: macOS on Apple M1 MacBook Air with 8 GB unified memory
environment.test_command: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib && bun run build && bun run lint && bun run format:check
environment.notes: The production backend is local Rust/Tauri, not a remote HTTP service. The current S1 engine already forces 99 Metal layers independently of the speech accelerator setting.

components.name: cleanup evidence and observability
components.description: Stage-level traces, typed outcomes, privacy-safe metrics, fixtures, and a reproducible benchmark that prove which transform produced the final text and where time is spent.

components.name: safe normalization boundary
components.description: A narrow post-S1 token canonicalization path that preserves exact technical terms and values without deterministic grammar, punctuation, casing, or broad common-word rewrites.

components.name: S1 model contract and validation
components.description: The exact trained S1 prompt, formal/lists/general controls, greedy decoding, per-chunk fidelity checks, explicit degradation reasons, and chunk-local fallback behavior.

components.name: incremental streaming cleanup
components.description: A recording-scoped scheduler that consumes monotonic committed ASR text, retains a revision tail, cleans stable chunks during capture, and finalizes only unresolved text at stop.

components.name: bounded Metal throughput
components.description: Measured selection and implementation of the fastest safe llama.cpp scheduling strategy on the target M1 without unbounded concurrency, duplicate model loads, swap, or ASR starvation.

components.name: ordered fidelity-safe assembly
components.description: Sequence-numbered result ordering, boundary handling, cancellation, backpressure, final reconciliation, and exact preservation invariants across chunks.

components.name: truthful frontend lifecycle
components.description: Existing Journal and recording surfaces show real ready, cleaning, finalizing, degraded, and unavailable states without implying success when S1 output was discarded.

components.name: quality and performance release gate
components.description: A repeatable target-hardware evaluation, before/after report, soak test, rollback criteria, and full project validation.

tasks.title: Make every cleanup stage and fallback measurable
tasks.description: Add a recording-scoped cleanup trace and separate internal/public outcome contracts before changing behavior. The internal CleanupResult carries final transcript text for paste and is never serialized. CleanupOutcomeSummary carries only privacy-safe state and metrics for status/events. Capture stage durations, token and chunk counts, queue wait, prompt evaluation, generation speed, validation result, and final source selection without logging transcript contents. Expose the latest aggregate state through the existing cleanup status command and a typed terminal event so a rejected model output can no longer masquerade as active cleanup.

Internal CleanupResult containing final_text and CleanupOutcomeSummary
Serializable CleanupOutcomeSummary with Applied, PartiallyApplied, Skipped, Rejected, Failed, and Cancelled lifecycle variants
CleanupRunMetrics with durations, input/output token counts, chunk counts, queue depth, backend, and fallback reason
Existing CleanupModelStatus command and Tauri cleanup lifecycle events
packages: existing log, serde, specta, tauri, and llama-cpp-2 crates only

files.what: Replace Option<String> job replies with CleanupOutcome and attach run IDs and aggregate metrics.
Own privacy-safe run metrics, reason codes, stage timing, and latest-status aggregation.
Return the real latest cleanup state and degraded reason in the existing status contract.
Register CleanupRunStatusEvent in the existing Specta collect_events list.
Regenerate typed CleanupModelStatus and cleanup event payloads through the existing Specta binding workflow.
Add sanitized raw-ASR fixtures for common-word casing, repetition, self-correction, numbers, code tokens, prose, and enumerations.

subtasks.description: Define internal CleanupResult { final_text: String, summary: CleanupOutcomeSummary } and serializable CleanupOutcomeSummary, CleanupRunId, CleanupFallbackReason, CleanupValidationReason, and CleanupRunMetrics types; final_text must not implement Specta event serialization.
Assign one run ID at the start of output handling and propagate it through enqueue, generation, validation, assembly, status, and final paste selection.
Record queue_wait_ms, prompt_eval_ms, generation_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, generated_tokens_per_second, chunk_index, chunk_count, and total_ms without recording transcript text.

Extend CleanupModelStatus with backend, lifecycle state, and last-run summary while preserving installed plus ready as active; define CleanupRunStatusEvent carrying the same privacy-safe summary and register it in lib.rs.
Emit CleanupRunStatusEvent exactly once for every terminal run and create sanitized fixtures derived from the reported TODAY, AND, RIGHT, repetitive prose, launch-list, and long-dictation failures.

tests.description: Unit-test every CleanupOutcome and reason-code serialization shape used by Specta and Tauri.
Integration-test an accepted candidate, a validation rejection, a not-ready engine, a timeout, and a non-English skip and assert the recorded final source.
Run one real short Metal cleanup and verify logs contain timing and reason fields but no transcript contents.

acceptance_criteria: Every cleanup attempt has one run ID and one terminal typed outcome.
A discarded S1 result is observable as Rejected or Failed and never reported as a successful active cleanup run.
The latest status remains real backend state and contains no fabricated frontend inference.
Metrics contain no raw transcript, model prompt, clipboard content, file content, API key, or other PII.
Only internal CleanupResult contains final_text; CleanupOutcomeSummary, CleanupModelStatus, logs, bindings, and Tauri events cannot contain transcript text.
Every terminal run emits one CleanupRunStatusEvent so mounted frontend consumers can refresh without polling.
The reported 2,584-character failure can be classified by a concrete validation reason instead of one generic warning.

tasks.title: Remove deterministic prose rewriting and unsafe global catalog aliases
tasks.description: Change the English path so S1 receives raw ASR text rather than text already rewritten by global styling/programming catalogs. Keep only meaning-preserving normalization after S1. Remove production calls that infer grammar, punctuation, capitalization, paragraphs, or Markdown. Prevent bare common English aliases from becoming SQL, spreadsheet, API, or shell tokens outside an explicitly detected technical span.
building_blocks: English CleanupInput containing raw ASR text plus language evidence
PostCleanupTokenNormalizer for explicit technical tokens and numeric/value normalization only
TechnicalSpan classifier requiring an unambiguous multiword or syntax-shaped cue
Existing tech_lexicon, styling, programming_syntax, normalize_values, custom words, and language evidence

files.what: Split raw ASR finalization from language-specific deterministic fallback and stop running global English prose catalogs before S1.
Run mandatory S1 on raw English ASR, then invoke only safe token normalization before optional downstream features.
Reject or context-gate ambiguous single-word aliases such as and, right, today, now, left, match, search, and filter.
Limit styling canonicalization to explicit class-shaped or multiword Tailwind utterances and never rewrite normal prose.
Keep numeric, currency, percentage, unit, date, and exact token normalization callable while deleting or leaving unreachable all production grammar, punctuation, casing, and list formatting paths.
Mark or remove ambiguous bare-prose aliases from globally eligible token substitutions while retaining the catalog as reference data.

subtasks.description: Introduce a raw-versus-normalized transcript boundary so the English S1 request is built from untouched ASR output.

Inventory all production callers of formatter::format, punctuation::punctuate, normalize_transcription_output, styling::apply, and programming_syntax::apply and remove English grammar/punctuation/casing callers.
Classify catalog aliases as globally_safe or technical_context_only; default ambiguous single English words to technical_context_only.
Require explicit evidence such as SQL query language, an HTTP request phrase, a formula marker, a file extension, a path, or a class prefix before applying technical_context_only aliases.
Apply approved technical and value normalization after S1 so ordinary English words are never injected into the model as uppercase syntax tokens.
Retain the existing non-English fallback branch and verify it does not run the English-only S1 model or English-only value rules.

tests.description: Regression-test the exact prose family: today, and, right, now, get, left, match, search, filter, sort, upper, lower, and trim remain normal sentence-case words.
Test explicit technical phrases such as GET request, RIGHT JOIN, SQL AND, TODAY(), DATABASE_URL, dot tsx, and bg stone 700 still normalize correctly.
Differential-test the English production path and prove no deterministic function adds sentence punctuation, title casing, headings, or lists before or after S1.
Run the existing non-English language tests unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: The reported ordinary prose never outputs TODAY, AND, RIGHT, or NOW unless the source explicitly contains those uppercase tokens or technical-span evidence requires them.
English grammar, punctuation, capitalization, paragraphing, filler cleanup, and list structure have one owner: S1-mini.
Safe normalization preserves exact code tokens, paths, file extensions, numbers, currency, percentages, units, dates, and negations without inventing them.
No JSON catalog is inserted into the S1 prompt.
Non-English dictation behavior remains unchanged and S1 remains skipped for unsupported languages.

tasks.title: Make the S1 contract exact and fallback chunk-local
tasks.description: Lock production inference to the model's trained interface and stop discarding an entire long transcript when one chunk fails. Interpret the dictated request for full formal cleanup as the valid S1 Styling formal control; keep Structure lists and Context general. Validate each chunk against the corresponding raw source and substitute only the failed chunk while reporting a partially applied outcome.
building_blocks: Exact system prompt and control line constants
CleanupChunkInput and CleanupChunkResult contracts
Greedy sampler with empty think block
Per-invariant validation reasons
Chunk-local raw fallback

files.what: Declare child modules and replace the all-or-nothing sequential outcome path.
Own exact S1 prompt constants, valid controls, typed chunk input/result, and terminal outcomes.
Own fidelity invariants and precise rejection reasons independently of model execution.
Token-counted chunk construction with source spans and stable sequence IDs.

subtasks.description: Set the exact control line to [Styling: formal] [Structure: lists] [Context: general] and retain the documented system prompt and empty think prefix verbatim.
Keep greedy sampling explicit on every generation call and reject any future configuration value outside the trained control vocabulary at compile time.
Replace the 500-word cap with tokenizer-derived input limits that include prompt overhead and output headroom under N_CTX.
Return validation reason codes for repetition, think leakage, invented code/path tokens, lost negation, lost exact numeric token, implausible truncation, and invalid UTF-8 repair.
Assemble accepted model chunks with source chunks substituted only where validation or generation failed and mark the run PartiallyApplied.
Treat an empty S1 result as valid only for filler/noise-only input; reject empty output for meaningful source content.

tests.description: Snapshot-test the exact trained prompt bytes, formal/lists/general control values, empty think block, and greedy sampler construction.
Tokenize boundary fixtures through the installed llama-cpp tokenizer and prove every prompt plus maximum output budget fits N_CTX.
Inject one rejected middle chunk between two accepted chunks and assert the accepted chunks survive while only the middle source span falls back.
Replay filler-only, prose, self-correction, number/date/currency, code-token, and three-item enumeration fixtures through the real Metal model.

acceptance_criteria: Production uses only trained S1 control values; no bullets, markdown, work, font-normal, or arbitrary prompt instructions are sent.
One failed chunk cannot discard successful cleanup for other chunks.
Every chunk is bounded by actual model tokens rather than an English word-count estimate.
Validation preserves meaning-critical tokens and produces an exact rejection reason.
The plan does not claim headings, bold, links, summaries, or guaranteed lists for non-enumerable prose.

tasks.title: Clean stable ASR commits during recording
tasks.description: Introduce a recording-scoped cleanup session beside the existing transcribe-cpp stream. Feed only monotonic committed text, never tentative text, into a token-aware segment assembler. Hold a small unresolved tail for cross-boundary self-corrections and list structure, enqueue stable chunks during capture, and reconcile against the finalized ASR text at stop.
building_blocks: CleanupSessionId tied to the existing streaming worker ID
Begin, Commit, Finish, and Cancel commands
Committed-prefix delta calculation keyed by stream revision
StableSegmentAssembler with retained revision tail
Finalization reply containing ordered cleaned chunks and unresolved tail
packages: existing std mpsc and tokio channels only

files.what: Own session commands, committed-prefix tracking, stable segment assembly, reconciliation, and cancellation.
Start, feed, finish, or cancel one cleanup session from the existing streaming lifecycle and committed_changed updates.
Consume the finalized cleanup session output instead of always issuing a new whole-transcript S1 request after stop.

subtasks.description: Define begin_session(session_id, language), push_committed(session_id, revision, committed_snapshot), finish_session(session_id, final_text), and cancel_session(session_id) contracts.
On each committed_changed update, verify the committed snapshot is monotonic, derive the new suffix, and ignore duplicate or stale revisions.
Accumulate actual model tokens and close a chunk at the strongest available boundary before the cap while retaining a configurable 40-to-80-token provisional tail.
Keep tentative ASR text visible in the overlay but out of S1 so changing hypotheses cannot create duplicate cleanup work.
At finalize, compare the concatenated committed source with final_text, invalidate only the first divergent provisional span, and enqueue the changed tail.
Propagate recording cancellation to queued and generating cleanup work and guarantee that a late result cannot enter a newer session.

tests.description: Feed synthetic committed and tentative update sequences and assert every committed source token is scheduled exactly once in order.
Test self-correction across a proposed boundary, including Friday no wait Thursday, and assert the correction remains in one provisional tail.
Test duplicate revisions, stale revisions, a non-monotonic final snapshot, cancel during generation, and immediate next-session start.
Replay a 10-minute and a 30-minute committed-stream trace and assert finish schedules only the unresolved tail under normal operation.

acceptance_criteria: S1 work starts during recording for streaming-capable English ASR instead of waiting for stop.
Tentative text is never cleaned, committed text is never duplicated, and source order is stable.
Cross-boundary self-corrections remain revisable until their retained tail is sealed.
Finish reuses completed chunks and submits only changed or unresolved text.
Cancel fully isolates sessions and produces no stale paste or status event.

tasks.title: Benchmark bounded llama.cpp scheduling on the target M1
tasks.description: Run a controlled experiment before choosing concurrency. Compare the current single reusable context, two shared-model contexts, and llama.cpp multi-sequence batching supported by llama-cpp-2 0.1.154. Measure aggregate generation throughput, per-chunk latency, prompt evaluation, ASR real-time factor, memory pressure, swap, and thermal behavior at concurrency 1, 2, 3, and 4. Select the smallest configuration that materially improves end-to-end latency without starving streaming ASR.
building_blocks: Existing tmp-s1bench fixture runner corrected to the production prompt
Production local_cleanup engine behind a benchmark-only adapter
llama-cpp-2 LlamaContextParams n_seq_max, n_batch, n_ubatch, and sequence IDs
One-model shared-weight experiment
Before/after benchmark report

files.what: Run production prompt, tokenizer, validation, chunking, and candidate schedulers against fixed fixtures.
Register the local benchmark binary without changing shipped runtime dependencies.
Record hardware, fixture hashes, exact commands, raw metrics, before/after table, and selected configuration.
Remove the stale invalid-control benchmark after the production-faithful Rust harness replaces it.

subtasks.description: Make the benchmark use the exact formal/lists/general prompt, greedy decoding, empty think block, production tokenizer budget, validator, and model path.
Measure serial one-context baseline over short, 2,584-character, 10-minute, and 30-minute fixtures with warm-up excluded and at least 10 measured repetitions per short case.
Prototype shared-model two-context scheduling and record whether LlamaModel sharing is safe and whether extra KV memory causes pressure or swap.
Prototype one-context multi-sequence batching using n_seq_max and sequence IDs and compare n_batch, n_ubatch, and flash-attention policy only where supported.
Run each candidate concurrently with live Parakeet streaming and reject any configuration that materially worsens ASR real-time factor, drops commits, causes memory pressure, or swaps.

Select bounded concurrency only if it improves aggregate cleanup throughput by at least 20 percent and stop-to-paste p95 by at least 15 percent with no quality failures; otherwise retain one worker and rely on incremental scheduling.

tests.description: Run identical fixture hashes through every candidate and assert byte-identical greedy output or record and reject semantic differences.
Measure concurrency 1 through 4 while Parakeet streams and capture p50, p95, aggregate tokens per second, ASR RTF, RSS, memory pressure, swap, and failures.
Repeat the winning configuration after a cold app start and after a 30-minute soak.

acceptance_criteria: benchmark-results.md contains reproducible commands, hardware, model hash, fixture hashes, raw samples, medians, p95 values, and a before/after table.
The plan never equates prompt-processing throughput with generation throughput; both are reported separately.
The selected strategy loads model weights once, has a hard concurrency cap, and creates no swap under the accepted workload.
Unbounded or merely higher concurrency is rejected when it harms end-to-end latency, ASR, memory, thermals, or quality.
If no parallel candidate clears the gate, one incremental worker is the documented production choice.

tasks.title: Integrate the measured Metal scheduler with backpressure
tasks.description: Implement only the scheduling strategy selected by T5. Keep the model permanently on Apple Metal and independent of the speech accelerator dropdown. Reuse one loaded model, bound active sequences and queued chunks, prioritize final-tail work over background commits, and preserve deterministic ordered output under completion reordering.
building_blocks: Measured SchedulerConfig frozen from benchmark results
Bounded high-priority final queue and normal committed queue
Context or sequence ownership guard
Per-session cancellation token
Ordered result channel
packages: existing llama-cpp-2 and tokio crates only

files.what: Own one Metal model, selected context or multi-sequence scheduler, greedy generation, and engine lifecycle.
Own bounded queues, priorities, fairness, cancellation, backpressure, and ordered completion delivery.
Delegate engine and scheduling work to focused modules while preserving install, readiness, and Tauri command entry points.

subtasks.description: Encode the T5 winner as explicit constants or a typed internal configuration with the benchmark report as its source of truth.
Initialize exactly one LlamaBackend and one LlamaModel with METAL_GPU_LAYERS independent of transcribe_accelerator and transcribe_gpu_device.
Implement the measured context or multi-sequence cap and enforce bounded queue capacity with explicit backpressure rather than dropping committed text.
Prioritize Finish tail jobs over background Commit jobs while retaining starvation-free progress for active recordings.
Attach session ID, sequence number, and cancellation generation to every job and ignore late cancelled completions.
On fatal engine failure set READY false, fail all pending replies exactly once, emit cleanup-model-failed, and allow the existing install or preload path to recover.

tests.description: Stress concurrent sessions and out-of-order completions and assert ordered, exactly-once result delivery with no deadlock.
Fill the queue to capacity, finalize one session, cancel another, and assert backpressure, priority, and cancellation behavior.
Toggle the speech accelerator among CPU, Auto, and GPU and verify cleanup status and logs continue to report Metal with identical S1 configuration.
Inject an engine failure and assert all waiters terminate, readiness becomes false, and no stale text is pasted.

acceptance_criteria: Cleanup always runs on Metal on supported macOS hardware regardless of speech accelerator selection.
Only the benchmark-approved number of contexts or sequences can execute concurrently.
One model weight allocation is shared; no worker reloads or duplicates the GGUF.
Queue saturation applies measurable backpressure and never silently drops source text.
Cancellation, failure, and restart paths terminate every request exactly once.

Carry boundary metadata from chunk construction and join chunks using source paragraph boundaries; never insert blank lines solely because a token cap was reached.

acceptance_criteria: Chunk completion order cannot change pasted text order.
Hard token chunking cannot create arbitrary blank paragraphs.
The overlay disappears immediately when background cleanup has already caught up and shows finalizing only for real tail work.
The Journal card remains minimal and reports installed plus ready as active, with degraded or unavailable state derived from the backend.
All frontend state is fully typed and all locale keys are complete.

tasks.title: Prove quality, latency, memory, and rollout safety
tasks.description: Run the complete production path on the target M1 using representative short, 2-to-5-minute, 10-minute, 20-minute, and 30-minute traces. Compare raw ASR, pre-S1 input, per-chunk S1 output, validator decisions, final text, queue metrics, and stop-to-paste latency. Ship only when invariant, human-quality, ASR coexistence, memory, and reliability gates pass; otherwise keep the previous release behind a rollback switch while fixing the failed gate.
building_blocks: Golden invariant suite
Blind human preference rubric
Long-session trace replay
Before/after performance table
Failure injection and soak test
Internal rollback flag removed after confidence window
tools: Bun build, lint, and format check

files.what: Expand the corpus to cover every reported regression and boundary invariant.
Store sanitized committed and tentative stream transitions for long-session replay.
Record final commands, fixture hashes, quality results, timing distributions, memory, failures, and go or no-go decision.
Remove temporary compatibility or rollback plumbing after the confidence window, or document the explicit no-go state.

subtasks.description: Build a sanitized corpus with conversational prose, profanity, repetitions, false starts, self-corrections, exact numbers, dates, currency, email, code tokens, paths, negations, three-item lists, non-lists, and filler-only audio.
Assert 100 percent invariant preservation for explicit numbers, currency, paths, extensions, identifiers, negations, source ordering, and no invented headings or code tokens.
Run blind A/B review against the current release and require at least an 80 percent preference for the new output with zero common-word ALL-CAPS regressions.

Measure stop-to-paste p50 and p95 by duration and require at most 1.5 seconds p50 and 3 seconds p95 for 10-minute streaming recordings, and at most 2.5 seconds p50 and 5 seconds p95 for 30-minute recordings when cleanup kept pace during capture.
Require cleanup backlog at stop to be at most one normal chunk plus the retained tail for steady-state recordings; separately report overload cases rather than hiding them.
Run 30-minute concurrent ASR plus cleanup soak tests and require no crash, deadlock, swap, stale session output, lost text, or ASR real-time-factor regression greater than 10 percent.
Run cargo fmt check, clippy with warnings denied where supported, the full Rust library suite, Bun build, lint, format check, translation check, and targeted Tauri smoke flows.
Write verification-report.md with every result and an explicit go, conditional-go, or no-go decision; do not claim completion for unrun or failed checks.

tests.description: Run the full invariant corpus through the same modules and engine used in production.
Run target-hardware 2-, 5-, 10-, 20-, and 30-minute stream replays and collect p50 and p95 metrics.
Inject validator rejection, queue saturation, cancellation, engine failure, not-ready state, and app restart during cleanup.

Run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib, cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check, cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings, bun run build, bun run lint, bun run format:check, and bun run check:translations.

acceptance_criteria: Zero fixture emits unexplained common-word ALL-CAPS tokens, invented paths or extensions, lost negations, reordered chunks, or repetition loops.
The S1 model is proven used or explicitly degraded for every English run; no silent fallback remains.
The long-stream stop-to-paste, backlog, ASR coexistence, memory, and reliability gates pass on the target M1 8 GB machine.
benchmark-results.md and verification-report.md distinguish prompt evaluation speed, generation speed, total latency, queue wait, and final tail latency.
All required Rust and frontend checks pass, or the report names the exact pre-existing or new blocker and the release remains no-go.
